# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/cli-reference.sh from `wasmkeep --help`: do not edit by hand. -->

Every command and flag of `wasmkeep`, with its default and a one-line meaning. The one-line
meaning is the first sentence of the flag's help; `wasmkeep <command> --help` prints the whole
text. This page is generated from the built binary, and `./scripts/cli-reference.sh --check` fails
when it is stale.

For how the flags fit together, see [Running a cluster](../cluster.md),
[the node file](node-file.md), [Socket admission options](socket-limits.md) and
[Going to production](../tutorials/going-to-production.md). For what to do when a node refuses to
start, see [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md).

Options before the command (`--malloc-arena-max`) apply to every command and are listed once, under `wasmkeep`.

## `wasmkeep`

Self-hosted actor platform for Wasm components

Usage: `wasmkeep [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--malloc-arena-max <MALLOC_ARENA_MAX>` | `cores, clamped to 2..8` | glibc arena cap before threads start; 0 preserves glibc/environment defaults. |

### `wasmkeep inspect`

Open a local, read-only bucket inspector

Usage: `wasmkeep inspect [OPTIONS] --app <APP>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--app <APP>` |  | App to inspect, TENANT/APP |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX]; defaults to WASMKEEP_BUCKET |
| `--bind <BIND>` | `127.0.0.1` | Bind only to 127.0.0.1 or ::1 |
| `--port <PORT>` | `0` | Local port; zero chooses a free port |

### `wasmkeep assets`

Collect unused static assets and expired versions from an app's bucket

Usage: `wasmkeep assets [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

#### `wasmkeep assets collect`

Collect old versions and unused contents and indexes (ADR 0030)

Usage: `wasmkeep assets collect [OPTIONS] --app <APP> --bucket <BUCKET>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--app <APP>` |  | The app, TENANT/APP |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] |
| `--version-retention-secs <SECS>` | `3600` | Minimum retention for old versions and unused assets, in seconds |

### `wasmkeep serve`

Serve actors (`/actor/<class>/<name>/...`) and/or a front: a stateless wasi:http component (one instance per request) for every other path, which calls the actors.

Usage: `wasmkeep serve [OPTIONS] [COMPONENT]`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `[COMPONENT]` | | The front: a stateless component (.wasm exporting wasi:http/incoming-handler) for every path outside /actor/ and /_wasmkeep/. It may call the --actor classes with actors.call, and read its values (--front-env) with env.get. |
| `--assets-cache-bytes <ASSETS_CACHE_BYTES>` | `1073741824` | Process-wide static asset disk cache ceiling in bytes |
| `--actor <CLASS=PATH>` |  | Actor class served at `/actor/<CLASS>/<name>/...`, as CLASS=PATH to a component implementing the wasmkeep:actor world. |
| `--data-dir <DATA_DIR>` | `.wasmkeep/data` | Where actor databases live |
| `--idle-timeout-secs <IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS>` | `30` | Seconds an idle actor stays in memory before hibernating |
| `--idle-memory-trim-secs <IDLE_MEMORY_TRIM_SECS>` | `60` | On Linux/glibc, sample actors + sockets every N seconds; trim at half the peak or zero, with a 60s minimum cooldown. |
| `--listen <LISTEN>` | `127.0.0.1:8080` | Address to listen on. |
| `--node-id <NODE_ID>` |  | Join a cluster as this node (`[a-z0-9-]`, unique per node). |
| `--app <APP>` |  | Serve the classes deployed for this app (TENANT/APP) with `wasmkeep deploy`, following new deploys. |
| `--node-file <FILE>` |  | Serve the apps a node file lists (`wasmkeep-node.toml`, ADR 0038): the listeners, the node id and every per-app setting come from the file, so their flags are refused beside it. |
| `--advertise <ADVERTISE>` |  | URL the other nodes reach this one at, e.g. http://10.0.0.11:8080 |
| `--cluster-listen <ADDR>` |  | Serve the cluster listener on this address (e.g. `0.0.0.0:7443`): the port other nodes use to reach this one, with mutual TLS 1.3 (each node's certificate is made in memory at start and pinned in its heartbeat; nothing to provision). |
| `--cluster-advertise <URL>` |  | URL the other nodes reach the cluster listener at, e.g. https://10.0.0.11:7443 (needs --cluster-listen) |
| `--cluster-plaintext <MODE>` | `refuse` | Plain HTTP between nodes. One of: accept, refuse. |
| `--history-retention-secs <SECS>` | `3600` | Seconds an actor's old history stays in the bucket before garbage collection may delete it (ADR 0012); 0 deletes it as soon as the rule allows. |
| `--no-idle-compaction` |  | Never compact an idle actor's history (ADR 0042): no snapshot at the head when an actor hibernates, and no idle pass a retention window later. |
| `--failover-wait-secs <SECS>` |  | Seconds a request for an actor whose node died or is stopping is kept until another node can take the actor over, instead of a 503 at once: a GET or HEAD without a body, or a WebSocket upgrade, arriving from outside. |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX]. Credentials, region and endpoint come from the AWS_* environment variables (AWS_ENDPOINT for MinIO or R2, AWS_ALLOW_HTTP=true for plain http) |
| `--cache-dir <CACHE_DIR>` | `.wasmkeep/cache` | Directory for pre-compiled components |
| `--max-instances <MAX_INSTANCES>` | `1000` | Maximum concurrently live instances (pooling allocator slots) |
| `--cpu-budget-ms <CPU_BUDGET_MS>` | `50` | Guest CPU time allowed per actor event, in milliseconds. |
| `--sql-cpu-budget-ms <SQL_CPU_BUDGET_MS>` | `2000` | CPU time one event's SQL statements may use together, in milliseconds (SQLite runs in the host, outside --cpu-budget-ms) |
| `--sqlite-heap-bytes <BYTES>` |  | SQLite's heap for the whole process, in bytes (default 4 GiB, at least 64 MiB), temporary data such as sorts included: past it, the statement that needs more fails with `quota-exceeded`. |
| `--usage-ping` |  | Send an anonymous usage report (version, OS, cluster or not, and bucketed counts of classes and resident actors) a minute after start and daily. |
| `--otlp-endpoint <OTLP_ENDPOINT>` |  | Export traces as OTLP/HTTP protobuf to this collector base URL. |
| `--trace-sample <TRACE_SAMPLE>` | `0.01` | Fraction of outside requests to trace (0 to 1), when an endpoint is set |
| `--trace-trust-incoming` |  | Honour both values of an incoming traceparent sampled flag |
| `--metrics-listen <ADDR>` |  | Serve Prometheus metrics at `http://ADDR/metrics` (e.g. `127.0.0.1:9100`). |
| `--metrics-host <NAME>` |  | A name the metrics page answers to, for a scraper that names this node by a dotted host name (`node1.internal`). |
| `--allow-outbound <CIDR>` |  | Let actors' outbound HTTP reach this non-public range (`10.0.0.0/8`, `127.0.0.1`, `fd00::/8`). |
| `--allow-outbound-port <PORT>` |  | Let actors' outbound HTTP use this port. |
| `--guest-log-rate <LINES>` | `50` | Lines a second each actor instance (and each front request) may print to the node's log, with bursts of twice that; past it, lines are dropped and counted. |
| `--transparent-huge-pages <MODE>` | `off` | Transparent huge pages for this process (Linux): `off` (the default) or `system` (whatever the kernel is set to). One of: off, system. |
| `--outbound-ca <FILE>` |  | Also trust this certificate authority (PEM) for actors' outbound HTTPS, besides the public ones: for an internal API behind a private CA. |
| `--max-connections <MAX_CONNECTIONS>` | `10000` | Client connections open at once; more wait until one closes |
| `--max-sockets-per-actor <MAX_SOCKETS_PER_ACTOR>` | `1000` | Socket sessions per actor owner; zero refuses all WebSockets at this scope |
| `--max-sockets-per-node <MAX_SOCKETS_PER_NODE>` |  | Process socket sessions, including relays; default 50,000, clamped to the FD budget. |
| `--max-sockets-per-app <MAX_SOCKETS_PER_APP>` |  | App socket sessions; defaults to the node cap. |
| `--env <CLASS=FILE>` |  | Configuration and secrets for a class, as CLASS=FILE: `NAME=value` lines its actors read with `env.get` (see docs/concepts.md). |
| `--front-env <FILE>` |  | The front's configuration and secrets on this node: `NAME=value` lines it reads with `env.get`, as --env gives a class's. |
| `--max-front-requests <N>` |  | Front requests running at once on this node; past it, 503 with `Retry-After: 1`. |
| `--max-blob-bytes <BYTES>` | `1073741824` | One file's largest size, in bytes, for a streamed write of an actor's or the front's files (ADR 0030): at most 5 GiB, one presigned PUT's ceiling on S3. |
| `--max-app-blob-bytes <BYTES>` |  | The app's stored-bytes limit (ADR 0030, section 7): once the hourly count of its files is over it, writes and upload links are refused with `quota-exceeded` until a count is under it again. |
| `--blob-links <BLOB_LINKS>` | `auto` | Links to actors' and the front's files (ADR 0030): `auto` presigns downloads on a bucket whose start proof passed and uses node links otherwise; `presigned` refuses to start when the proof fails; `node`: node links only. One of: auto, presigned, node. |
| `--blob-link-endpoint <URL>` |  | The bucket's endpoint as browsers reach it, for presigned links (default: the one this node uses, `AWS_ENDPOINT` or the provider's). |
| `--blob-link-base <URL>` |  | Where node links point, `https://HOST[:PORT]` (no path): by default `https://` and the app's first hostname, else --advertise. |
| `--no-alarms` |  | Never fire an actor's alarms on this node: no delivery, no sweep of the cluster's alarm index. |
| `--no-placement` |  | Never send a wake-up of an actor nobody holds to a lighter node, nor receive one (ADR 0041): this process's node ids keep every actor they wake and do not announce `place`. |
| `--writes <CLASS=MODE>` |  | How a class given with --actor writes, as CLASS=MODE: `strict` (the default) or `batched` (ADR 0034: plain writes are uploaded behind the events). |
| `--max-unsent-age <MS>` | `500` | How long a committed write of a batched class may wait unsent behind the segment in flight, in milliseconds, before its actor stops starting events (ADR 0034, section 3): 100 to 5000 |
| `--front-cpu-budget-ms <MS>` | `50` | The front's CPU time per request, in milliseconds (apart from --cpu-budget-ms, the actors'). |
| `--secrets-key <FILE>` |  | The app's secrets key (`wasmkeep secrets new-key`), with `--app`: secrets set with `wasmkeep secrets` reach `env.get`, over the deployed configuration and under `--env` (ADR 0016). |
| `--no-secrets` |  | With `--app`, run without the app's secrets from the bucket (`--env` only). |
| `--access <CLASS=MODE>` |  | Who may reach a class from outside, as CLASS=MODE: `open` (the default: any request, and a new name creates the actor), `existing` (only actors that exist; other actors create them with actors.call), `existing:NAME,...` (also lets outside ... |

### `wasmkeep dev`

Build actor crates, serve them, and rebuild and hot-swap them on every source change.

Usage: `wasmkeep dev [OPTIONS] [CRATES]...`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `[CRATES]...  Actor crate directories (each with a Cargo.toml using wasmkeep-sdk). Without any, the project file (./wasmkeep.toml, or --project) is run: its front and classes, as deployed (ADR 0026)` | |  |
| `--project <PATH>` |  | The project file: a wasmkeep.toml, or a directory holding one |
| `--no-project` |  | Ignore ./wasmkeep.toml (with crate directories) |
| `--listen <LISTEN>` |  | Address to listen on (default 127.0.0.1:8080, or the project file's [dev] port) |
| `--data-dir <DATA_DIR>` |  | Where actor databases live while developing (default .wasmkeep/dev; with a project file, its [dev] data-dir, or .wasmkeep/dev beside the file) |
| `--poll-ms <POLL_MS>` | `500` | How often to check the sources for changes, in milliseconds |
| `--allow-outbound <CIDR>` |  | Let actors' outbound HTTP reach this non-public range, as with `serve` (for a local API: `--allow-outbound 127.0.0.1`). |
| `--allow-outbound-port <PORT>` |  | Let actors' outbound HTTP use this port, which is otherwise blocked, as with `serve` (e.g. 587 for a mail relay). |
| `--guest-log-rate <LINES>` | `50` | Lines a second each actor instance may print to the node's log, as with `serve`; 0 discards what actors print |
| `--transparent-huge-pages <MODE>` | `off` | Transparent huge pages for this process (Linux): `off` (the default) or `system` (whatever the kernel is set to). One of: off, system. |
| `--outbound-ca <FILE>` |  | Also trust this certificate authority (PEM) for actors' outbound HTTPS, besides the public ones: for an internal API behind a private CA. |
| `--env <CLASS=FILE>` |  | Configuration and secrets for a class, as CLASS=FILE: `NAME=value` lines its actors read with `env.get` (see docs/concepts.md). |
| `--access <CLASS=MODE>` |  | Who may reach a class from outside, as CLASS=MODE: `open` (the default: any request, and a new name creates the actor), `existing` (only actors that exist; other actors create them with actors.call), `existing:NAME,...` (also lets outside ... |

### `wasmkeep deploy`

Upload actor classes to the bucket and make them the version every node serving the app runs (`serve --app`).

Usage: `wasmkeep deploy [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--app <APP>` |  | The app, as TENANT/APP. |
| `--project <PATH>` |  | The project file (ADR 0026): a wasmkeep.toml, or a directory holding one. |
| `--no-project` |  | Ignore ./wasmkeep.toml: deploy with flags only |
| `--no-build` |  | With a project file, do not run its build commands (components built in an earlier step) |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables) |
| `--actor <CLASS=PATH>` |  | Actor class to deploy, as CLASS=PATH. |
| `--access <CLASS=MODE>` |  | Who may reach a class from outside, as CLASS=MODE (`open`, `existing`, `existing:NAME,...`, `internal`; see `serve --access`). |
| `--config <CLASS=FILE>` |  | Plain configuration for a class, as CLASS=FILE (`NAME=value` lines, read with `env.get`). |
| `--requires <CLASS=NAMES>` |  | Names a class requires among its values, as CLASS=NAME,NAME... (ADR 0016): while one is not set (by the configuration, the app's secrets or a node's --env), the class refuses its events with 503 instead of running without it. |
| `--front <PATH>` |  | The app's front (ADR 0023): a stateless `wasi:http` component (.wasm exporting wasi:http/incoming-handler) that receives every request outside /actor/ and calls the app's actors. |
| `--no-front` |  | Remove the front (with its configuration and required names): requests outside /actor/ then answer 404 |
| `--front-config <FILE>` |  | The front's plain configuration, as --config is a class's (stored in the clear: never secrets). |
| `--front-requires <NAMES>` |  | Names the front requires among its values, as --requires is a class's: while one is not set, the front answers 503. |
| `--assets <ASSETS>` |  | Static files to deploy (ADR 0030) |
| `--no-assets` |  | Remove static assets from the new version |
| `--assets-not-found <ASSETS_NOT_FOUND>` |  |  One of: front, spa, 404. |
| `--assets-front-first <ASSETS_FRONT_FIRST>` |  |  |
| `--assets-immutable <ASSETS_IMMUTABLE>` |  |  |
| `--assets-verify` |  | Download asset objects to detect and repair same-size corruption |
| `--yes` |  | Confirm a changed deploy with assets without an interactive prompt |
| `--rollback` |  | Go back to the version deployed before the current one, with its access rules, configuration and front |
| `--allow-reopen` |  | Let a rollback make a class more open (refused otherwise) |
| `--expire-after-idle <CLASS=DURATION>` |  | How long a class's actors may stay idle before they are deleted, as CLASS=DURATION (`7d`, `36h`, `90m`; at least 1h) (ADR 0028): in a cluster, an actor with no event for that long, no pending alarm and no open WebSocket is deleted. |
| `--writes <CLASS=MODE>` |  | How a class's plain writes reach the bucket, as CLASS=MODE: `strict` (each event's writes before the next event, the default) or `batched` (several events to a segment, ADR 0034). |
| `--recreate` |  | Deploy to an app deleted with `wasmkeep app delete`: its tombstone is removed first, only if nothing else of it is left in the bucket |
| `--version-retention-secs <SECS>` | `3600` | Seconds an old version stays in the bucket before this command may delete it (ADR 0012). |

### `wasmkeep cluster`

Inspect or steer a cluster through its bucket

Usage: `wasmkeep cluster [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

#### `wasmkeep cluster status`

Show the cluster under a bucket prefix, read from the bucket alone (no node needs to answer): each node's heartbeat (version, app, addresses, TLS pin, age, live or not), each app's deployed version, and each app's upgrade floor with the state of its upgrade (`finalize pending` once every live node runs the new version).

Usage: `wasmkeep cluster status [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables; read access is enough) |
| `--json` |  | Print JSON instead of tables, for scripts |

#### `wasmkeep cluster drain`

Ask a node to drain: stop taking actors and hand its own to other nodes of the same app (ADR 0014).

Usage: `wasmkeep cluster drain [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> [NODE]`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `[NODE]  The node's id` | |  |
| `--process <ID>` |  | Every node id this process runs (ADR 0038: the `process=` its heartbeats name), instead of one node. |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables) |
| `--force` |  | Write (or withdraw) the request even though no live node has the id (and, for `undrain`, no request names it) |

#### `wasmkeep cluster undrain`

Withdraw a drain request: the node takes actors again

Usage: `wasmkeep cluster undrain [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> [NODE]`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `[NODE]  The node's id` | |  |
| `--process <ID>` |  | Every node id this process runs (ADR 0038: the `process=` its heartbeats name), instead of one node. |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables) |
| `--force` |  | Write (or withdraw) the request even though no live node has the id (and, for `undrain`, no request names it) |

#### `wasmkeep cluster fence`

Fence a node (ADR 0020): its process stops at its next heartbeat write, and the actors it held are free 15 s after its last one (a lease's ttl plus grace, the defaults).

Usage: `wasmkeep cluster fence [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> <NODE>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<NODE>  The node's id` | |  |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables) |

#### `wasmkeep cluster forget`

Remove a retired node's heartbeat in the format from before node leases, or a released node lease no ownership record names, once it is older than 25 s (its horizon plus a lease's ttl and grace).

Usage: `wasmkeep cluster forget [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> <NODE>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<NODE>  The node's id` | |  |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables) |

#### `wasmkeep cluster upgrade`

Follow and end an upgrade of WasmKeep itself, one node at a time: `status` shows each node's version, each app's upgrade floor and what blocks a finalize; `finalize` ends the upgrade

Usage: `wasmkeep cluster upgrade [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

#### `wasmkeep cluster upgrade status`

Show the upgrade of WasmKeep itself, per app, read from the bucket alone: each registered node with its version, the app's upgrade floor (the lowest version allowed to serve it), one state (`one version`, `mixed`, `finalize pending`, `no live node`, `node below the floor`, `refused`) and the nodes that block a finalize.

Usage: `wasmkeep cluster upgrade status [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables; read access is enough) |
| `--app <APP>` |  | One app, TENANT/APP, instead of every app with registered nodes |
| `--json` |  | Print JSON instead of text, for scripts |

#### `wasmkeep cluster upgrade finalize`

End an upgrade: raise each app's upgrade floor to this `wasmkeep`'s minor version, so that no node of an older version starts again (there is no way back).

Usage: `wasmkeep cluster upgrade finalize [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables) |
| `--app <APP>` |  | One app, TENANT/APP, instead of every app with registered nodes |
| `--yes` |  | Write the floor; without it, print what would be done and exit with 2 |

#### `wasmkeep cluster diagnose`

Check that a bucket does what WasmKeep needs from it: conditional creates and replaces, reads and listings that follow writes and deletes, large objects, last-modified times and the clock.

Usage: `wasmkeep cluster diagnose [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket to check: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables, as for `serve`). |
| `--prefix-for-test <PREFIX>` | `diagnose` | Where under PREFIX the checks write: each run writes in its own `run-<ms>-<pid>/` folder below it, deleted afterwards, so two runs never share one. |
| `--skip-paging` |  | Skip the listing of 1,001 keys (1,001 small writes and as many deletes) |
| `--skip-links` |  | Skip the `blob-links` checks (presigned download links) |
| `--link-endpoint <URL>` |  | The bucket's endpoint as browsers reach it, for the `blob-links` checks (default: as for `serve`) |
| `--json` |  | Print JSON instead of lines, for scripts |

#### `wasmkeep cluster verify`

Check that a cluster's bucket is whole, reading it and never writing (it is not `backup verify`, which checks a backup's own contents, nor `cluster diagnose`, which checks what the bucket's API does): every actor can be restored from what the bucket holds, and the records around the actors read.

Usage: `wasmkeep cluster verify [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables; read access is enough, and no write is ever sent) |
| `--app <APP>` |  | One app, TENANT/APP, instead of every app under the prefix |
| `--actor <CLASS/NAME>` |  | One actor of --app, CLASS/NAME: its history and its ownership record, nothing else |
| `--sample <N>` |  | Read the ownership record (and with --deep the history) of N actors of each app, chosen at random, instead of every actor (the listing is still whole, so every actor's chain is still checked by its key names) |
| `--deep` |  | Also read every history object a restore would read and check its checksums (without --deep, damage inside one is not found), the previous versions a deploy keeps, and each static asset. |
| `--json` |  | Print JSON instead of text, for scripts |

### `wasmkeep actor`

Act on one actor of a cluster, through its bucket

Usage: `wasmkeep actor [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

#### `wasmkeep actor history`

List retained history without taking ownership

Usage: `wasmkeep actor history [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> <TENANT/APP> <ACTOR>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<TENANT/APP>` | |  |
| `<ACTOR>` | |  |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  |  |
| `--deep` |  |  |
| `--json` |  |  |

#### `wasmkeep actor export`

Export a verified, portable SQLite database from bucket history.

Usage: `wasmkeep actor export [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> --output <FILE> <TENANT/APP> <ACTOR>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<TENANT/APP>  Actor's app, TENANT/APP` | |  |
| `<ACTOR>       Actor address, CLASS/NAME` | |  |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX]; endpoint, region and credentials from AWS_* |
| `--at <AT>` |  | Capture-time boundary: RFC3339 or relative -15m, -2h, -1d. |
| `--txid <TXID>` |  | Exact retained transaction boundary on the current ancestry |
| `--max-bytes <MAX_BYTES>` | `2147483648` | Maximum replayed database bytes (twice the default server cap) |
| `--tmpdir <DIR>` |  | Parent directory for the plaintext scratch copy |
| `--require-owner-match` |  | Refuse an unavailable or mismatched owner hint (exit 3). |
| `-o, --output <FILE>` |  | New output SQLite file; existing files are never overwritten |

#### `wasmkeep actor sql`

Run one read-only SQL statement on a temporary, verified actor export

Usage: `wasmkeep actor sql [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> <TENANT/APP> <ACTOR> <QUERY>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<TENANT/APP>  Actor's app, TENANT/APP` | |  |
| `<ACTOR>       Actor address, CLASS/NAME` | |  |
| `<QUERY>       One read-only statement. Host/schema tables and PRAGMAs are denied` | |  |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX]; endpoint, region and credentials from AWS_* |
| `--at <AT>` |  | Capture-time boundary: RFC3339 or relative -15m, -2h, -1d. |
| `--txid <TXID>` |  | Exact retained transaction boundary on the current ancestry |
| `--max-bytes <MAX_BYTES>` | `2147483648` | Maximum replayed database bytes (twice the default server cap) |
| `--tmpdir <DIR>` |  | Parent directory for the plaintext scratch copy |
| `--require-owner-match` |  | Refuse an unavailable or mismatched owner hint (exit 3). |
| `--format <FORMAT>` |  | Output format (default: table on a terminal, csv otherwise) One of: table, csv, tsv, json, jsonl. |

#### `wasmkeep actor move`

Move an actor to NODE (ADR 0017): its owner hands it over, or NODE takes it if nobody holds it, within a few seconds.

Usage: `wasmkeep actor move [OPTIONS] --to <TO> --bucket <BUCKET> <ACTOR>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<ACTOR>  The actor: CLASS/NAME with `--app`, or `default/CLASS/NAME` for the implicit app `default/default` (the name may contain `/`)` | |  |
| `--app <APP>` |  | The actor's app, TENANT/APP; `default/default` (classes given on the command line) when the actor is written `default/CLASS/NAME` |
| `--to <TO>` |  | The node to move it to |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables) |
| `--force` |  | Write the request even though no live node has the id (one about to start, say) |

#### `wasmkeep actor delete`

Delete an actor (ADR 0028): its owner, or any node serving its class if nobody holds it, closes its WebSockets with 1000, removes its data and alarm, and records the delete in the bucket.

Usage: `wasmkeep actor delete [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> <ACTOR>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<ACTOR>  The actor: CLASS/NAME with `--app`, or `default/CLASS/NAME` for the implicit app `default/default` (the name may contain `/`)` | |  |
| `--resume <RESUME>` |  | Resume this operation ID without submitting another request |
| `--app <APP>` |  | The actor's app, TENANT/APP; `default/default` (classes given on the command line) when the actor is written `default/CLASS/NAME` |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables) |
| `--wait <WAIT>` | `60` | How long to wait for the delete to be recorded, in seconds (at most 3000: the request expires after an hour) |
| `--no-wait` |  | Write the request and return at once |

#### `wasmkeep actor restore`

Restore historical state as a new write by the current owner

Usage: `wasmkeep actor restore [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> <ACTOR>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<ACTOR>  CLASS/NAME (or default/CLASS/NAME without --app)` | |  |
| `--resume <RESUME>` |  | Resume this operation ID without submitting another request |
| `--app <APP>` |  |  |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  |  |
| `--txid <TXID>` |  |  |
| `--at <AT>` |  |  |
| `--from <FROM>` |  | Backup destination instead of live history |
| `--run <RUN>` |  |  |
| `--if-head <IF_HEAD>` |  | Refuse if the owner's flushed head changed (GEN:TXID) |
| `--wait <WAIT>` | `60` | Seconds to wait for an outcome (maximum 3000); requests expire after 50 minutes |
| `--no-wait` |  | Return immediately; the request remains live for 50 minutes |

#### `wasmkeep actor where`

Show which node owns each actor, whether that node is live and since when (read from the actor's ownership record and the heartbeats; an actor with no owner is "not placed").

Usage: `wasmkeep actor where [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> <ACTORS>...`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<ACTORS>...  The actors: CLASS/NAME with `--app`, or `default/CLASS/NAME` for the implicit app `default/default` (the name may contain `/`)` | |  |
| `--app <APP>` |  | The actors' app, TENANT/APP; `default/default` when an actor is written `default/CLASS/NAME` |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables; read access is enough) |
| `--json` |  | Print JSON instead of a table, for scripts |

### `wasmkeep secrets`

An app's secrets, sealed in the bucket (ADR 0016).

Usage: `wasmkeep secrets [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

#### `wasmkeep secrets new-key`

Write a new secrets key to FILE (64 hex characters, mode 0600; an existing file is refused).

Usage: `wasmkeep secrets new-key [OPTIONS] --out <OUT>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--out <OUT>` |  | The file to create |

#### `wasmkeep secrets set`

Set a secret (value from stdin, one trailing newline removed), or several from `--file`, as one change

Usage: `wasmkeep secrets set [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> --app <APP> --key <KEYS> [NAME]`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `[NAME]  The secret's name (its value is read from stdin)` | |  |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables) |
| `--app <APP>` |  | The app, as TENANT/APP |
| `--key <KEYS>` |  | The secrets key file. |
| `--force` |  | Change the secrets even while a live node of the app does not read them from the bucket (it would serve them as unset) |
| `--nodes-have-new-key` |  | With two keys, the first seals: say every node already has it when it is not the key the current set is sealed with (a node without it answers 503 for the app) |
| `--class <CLASS>` |  | The class, with NAME (value from stdin) |
| `--front` |  | The front's secret NAME (ADR 0023), read with `env.get` by the app's front (value from stdin) |
| `--file <FILE>` |  | Several secrets at once, in the sealed format (`<class> <name> <length>\n<value>\n` per secret; `_front` as the class for the front's) |

#### `wasmkeep secrets unset`

Remove secrets from a class or the front

Usage: `wasmkeep secrets unset [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> --app <APP> --key <KEYS> <NAMES>...`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<NAMES>...  The names to remove` | |  |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables) |
| `--app <APP>` |  | The app, as TENANT/APP |
| `--key <KEYS>` |  | The secrets key file. |
| `--force` |  | Change the secrets even while a live node of the app does not read them from the bucket (it would serve them as unset) |
| `--nodes-have-new-key` |  | With two keys, the first seals: say every node already has it when it is not the key the current set is sealed with (a node without it answers 503 for the app) |
| `--class <CLASS>` |  | The class |
| `--front` |  | Remove the front's secrets (ADR 0023) instead of a class's |

#### `wasmkeep secrets list`

List classes (and the front's scope, `_front`) and names (never values) and the current seq

Usage: `wasmkeep secrets list [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> --app <APP> --key <KEYS>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables) |
| `--app <APP>` |  | The app, as TENANT/APP |
| `--key <KEYS>` |  | The secrets key file. |
| `--force` |  | Change the secrets even while a live node of the app does not read them from the bucket (it would serve them as unset) |
| `--nodes-have-new-key` |  | With two keys, the first seals: say every node already has it when it is not the key the current set is sealed with (a node without it answers 503 for the app) |

#### `wasmkeep secrets rotate-key`

Re-seal an app's secrets under a new key (`--all`: every app under the prefix).

Usage: `wasmkeep secrets rotate-key [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> --new-key <NEW_KEY>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] |
| `--app <APP>` |  | The app, as TENANT/APP (or `--all`) |
| `--all` |  | Every app under the prefix that has secrets |
| `--key <KEY>` |  | The key the secrets are sealed with now |
| `--new-key <NEW_KEY>` |  | The key to seal them with (with `--finish`: the key to keep) |
| `--nodes-have-new-key` |  | Every node of the app already has the new key (`serve --secrets-key`, given twice during the change). |
| `--finish` |  | The last step, once the old key is removed from every node: delete every sealed object another key sealed, so the old key opens nothing left in the bucket. |

#### `wasmkeep secrets reset`

Write a whole set from a file without opening the current one: recovery after losing the key.

Usage: `wasmkeep secrets reset [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET> --app <APP> --new-key <NEW_KEY> --from <FROM>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] |
| `--app <APP>` |  | The app, as TENANT/APP |
| `--new-key <NEW_KEY>` |  | The key to seal with |
| `--from <FROM>` |  | The whole set, in the sealed format |
| `--force` |  | Reset even while a live node of the app does not read secrets |
| `--nodes-have-new-key` |  | Every node of the app already has the new key (`serve --secrets-key`, given twice during the change). |

### `wasmkeep new`

Write a new project into an empty directory: a class (a counter), optionally a front, its wasmkeep.toml, a README, .gitignore and an .env.local example.

Usage: `wasmkeep new [OPTIONS] --lang <LANG> <DIR>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<DIR>  The directory to write the project in: created if it does not exist, refused if it is not empty` | |  |
| `--lang <LANG>` |  | The language of the class and of the front One of: rust, typescript. |
| `--front` |  | Add a front: a page and an API over the class, which then stays `internal` (only the front reaches it). |
| `--app <TENANT/APP>` |  | TENANT/APP for `[app]` (each `[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}`). |

### `wasmkeep app`

Act on a whole app, through its bucket

Usage: `wasmkeep app [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

#### `wasmkeep app delete`

Delete an app (ADR 0028): writes its tombstone first, from which deploys refuse the app and its nodes stop serving it within a few seconds (closing its WebSockets with 1001); then, once no live node of the app is left, removes every key under its two prefixes: every actor's history, the ownership records, the alarm index, the requests, every deployed version and the sealed secrets.

Usage: `wasmkeep app delete [OPTIONS] --app <APP> --bucket <BUCKET>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--resume <RESUME>` |  | Resume this operation ID without submitting another request |
| `--app <APP>` |  | The app, TENANT/APP |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables) |
| `--wait <SECS>` | `60` | How long to wait for the app's live nodes to stop, in seconds; still live then, the command stops with the tombstone written and nothing removed (run it again) |
| `--force` |  | Remove the data even though nodes of the app still look live: only after `wasmkeep cluster fence` of each of them |

#### `wasmkeep app format`

Show the app's ownership-format setting (ADR 0035): version 1 records, the recorded-head format enabled, or an unreadable setting; with --enable, switch the app to the recorded-head format, one way, once every registered node of it announces `recorded-head` and none runs it

Usage: `wasmkeep app format [OPTIONS] --app <APP> --bucket <BUCKET>`

| Flag or argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--app <APP>` |  | The app, TENANT/APP |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` |  | Bucket shared by the cluster: s3://BUCKET[/PREFIX] (credentials from the AWS_* environment variables) |
| `--enable` |  | Enable the recorded-head format (cannot be undone): refused while a registered node of the app does not announce `recorded-head`, while one runs the app, and within the late-write window after the last stopped |
